skills.name: Code Review
skills.desc: Two-axis review of your diff: one pass against the repo's documented standards, one against the spec the work was meant to satisfy. The two run in parallel so neither colours the other.
skills.attribution: Built on the MIT-licensed review flow by Matt Pocock
skills.includes: Both review passes as separate runnable skills, the standards checklist, and the fixed-point workflow. Updates for a year.
ships: run-review.ps1 - pins the fixed point, proves the diff is non-empty, finds the standards and spec sources, emits both briefs
standards-checklist.md - the 12 Fowler smells as a printable checklist
verify-pack.ps1 - checks the pack installed correctly
worked-example/ - a real two-axis report and the run that produced it

proof.testedOn: The Register's own repository, 2 commits, 4 files
proof.result: The Spec axis caught a live defect. Three assertions in the render test still asserted the old contact address while the site had already moved to a new one - 166 of 169 checks were failing. Rewritten to read the address from skills.json instead of hardcoding it; 171 of 171 now pass, and two mutation tests confirm the new checks fail when the address is wrong.
proof.reproduce: Run the runner against any ref, hand brief-standards.md and brief-spec.md to two agents in parallel, paste both reports into REPORT.md. The report skeleton refuses to merge the axes.

skills.name: Grill With Docs
skills.desc: A relentless interview that sharpens a plan while it is still cheap to change, and leaves the decisions behind in a glossary and a stack of decision records.

skills.name: Test-Driven Development
skills.desc: The red-green-refactor loop, enforced. One failing test at a time, written before the code that makes it pass, and a full suite before the branch is called done.

skills.name: Prototype
skills.desc: Throwaway code with one job: answer a single design question you cannot settle on paper. Logic variant or interface variant, built to be discarded.
skills.attribution: Built on the MIT-licensed prototype skill by Matt Pocock
skills.includes: Both branches of the prototype skill - the logic harness and the interface variations - and the throwaway rules that stop it turning into production code. Updates for a year.
ships: new-prototype.ps1 - scaffolds a prototype with the one question written into it
verify-throwaway.ps1 - fails if anything outside the prototype folder imports it
worked-example/ - a real scaffold, and the guard firing on a real escape

proof.testedOn: A scratch repository with a src/ folder and one production file
proof.command: new-prototype.ps1 -Name pricing-tiers -Question 'Does a three-tier card grid fit 390px without a carousel?'
proof.result: Scaffolded three files with the question written into THROWAWAY.md, so the prototype cannot sprawl without someone noticing. The guard was then tested both ways: with a production import of the prototype planted it exited 1 and named the offending file and line; with the import removed it exited 0. A counting bug in the guard's own output was found by running it and fixed.
proof.reproduce: Scaffold a prototype, add an import of it from src/, run verify-throwaway.ps1 and read the exit code. Then remove the import and run it again.
